about:
# Twitch Emotes WoW Forever

Animated emotes, a searchable visual browser, and chat completion for every live World of
Warcraft client: Retail, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Anniversary, Classic Era, and WoW Forever.

## In game

Open the window with `/te`, `/twitch`, or the minimap button. Browse channel groups,
search by name, save favorites, or revisit recently sent emotes. Each Twitch channel
has one group; provider-wide emotes appear under **General**. General, Graycen,
Forsen, Erobb221, xQc, and Asmongold start enabled. The first time you enter the world
with the addon, the window opens on a welcome page with the channel picker, two seconds
after the loading screen lifts; it waits out combat, a cinematic or hidden interface,
death, and open dialogs. Each channel shows how many emotes
it has and a few samples; your current choices are already checked and every change
applies at once. **Finish**, the close button, Escape, or switching tabs ends it for
good; closing it also prints where to find the picker again. Players upgrading from an
earlier version who never pressed Done see it once too. Use **Channels** or
**Settings > Choose channels** to change the selection later.
Browse and search any installed channel, including disabled ones. Its **Enabled in
chat** checkbox controls display without leaving Browse. Enabled channels have a
purple highlight and checkmark in the group list.

Open chat, then click an emote (Shift-click when the line is empty) to insert its plain name.
Type a colon followed by at least two characters of a name to see suggestions with emote image
previews in the addon's own popup; Tab inserts the highlighted one, the arrow keys move the
highlight, a click picks any row, and Enter always sends the line as typed. Escape closes chat as
it always does (the line is cleared), so to leave the list just keep typing. Hover over a chat
emote for its name and source; Shift-click to insert it.
The addon sends ordinary text, so other players do not need it to read your messages.

Click an emote in chat for its menu, then choose **Hide this emote** to display that
name as ordinary text across channels and remove it from autocomplete.
Restore individual names under **Browse > Hidden**
or **Settings > Hidden emotes**. Shift-click still inserts a name into your draft.
Every Twitch global text face (`:)`, `:-P`, `:/`, `<3`, `O_o`, `B)` and the rest), `D:`, and the
chat words `1G`, `BOP`, `Retail`, and `Classic` start hidden. Restoring one overrides that default.

The purple and charcoal window includes a channel sidebar and a channel picker.
Additional channels can be enabled individually. When names overlap,
Settings lets you choose a preferred channel for the image. Identical provider
artwork shares a single texture file across packs.

Settings include an emote-size slider with a live preview (12–40 pixels, 28 by default),
chat channels, enabled groups, animation, the playback
limit (15, 30, or 60 FPS; 60 by default), and minimap visibility. Drag the minimap button to move it.
Minimap button collectors such as MinimapButtonButton, Leatrix Plus and EllesmereUI can gather the
button: when another addon has loaded LibDBIcon, the button registers there (as `TwitchEmotes`, also a
LibDataBroker launcher); otherwise the addon draws its own button, named `TwitchEmotesMinimapButton`.
Neither library is bundled.
Animation follows each source's timing; the playback limit cannot add motion absent
from the source. A hovered chat line pauses its animation to keep the tooltip stable;
other visible lines keep animating. Editor completion and insertion pause when WoW restricts scripted
chat input.

## Install

Place the `TwitchEmotes` folder in the client's `Interface/AddOns` directory (`_retail_`,
`_classic_`, `_anniversary_`, `_classic_era_`, or `_forever_`). Keep the folder name
`TwitchEmotes`. One install serves every client: each game type reads its own manifest
(`TwitchEmotes_Standard.toc` for Retail, `_Camelot` for Forever, `_Mists`, `_TBC`, `_Vanilla`;
`_Mainline` is the family fallback Retail and Forever share, and `TwitchEmotes.toc` the last
resort), all listing the same files and each titled for its game version in the AddOn List,
such as "Twitch Emotes (Classic Era)". The Interface numbers are the live builds the release
was audited against: 120105, 50504, 20506, 11509, and 16001.
**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing 3.2.1**, including updates from an earlier
build: `/reload` alone can leave newly installed textures as green boxes until the client
restarts. Later Lua-only updates take `/reload`; new textures or a changed TOC require a
restart. Preferences and usage are saved in `ForeverEmotesDB`, one table per client. Since
3.0.1 the addon keeps existing 3.x preferences and usage counts and imports nothing from
other emote addons.
If preferences reset, `/te status` reports the settings received during startup and
whether the active settings still match WoW's saved table. Early WoW Forever beta
clients never loaded saved addon settings; the live client does, so finishing the
first-run picker is remembered there as on every other client.

## Development

The runtime uses native WoW controls and chat filters. A literal matcher protects
links and URLs. A bounded message cache shares work between chat windows. Animation
updates only visible animated lines and stops its timer when no work remains. The
browser recycles its visible rows.

Provider artwork is downloaded and converted by `scripts/build-7tv-pack.py`. It
uses 64-pixel frames, up to 256 animation frames per sprite grid, and provider
originals at the highest offered resolution. It requires Python 3 and Pillow. Run `python3 scripts/build-7tv-pack.py --help` for pack
and cache options. Generated source records and hashes live in `packs/`.

After rebuilding packs, run `.venv/bin/python scripts/optimize-textures.py --budget BYTES`
from a virtual environment built with `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r
scripts/requirements-build.txt` (Pillow, numpy, imagequant, and the optional libdeflate
binding, which sizes candidates the way the release ZIP compresses them; zlib level 9
stands in without it). The optimizer reads every lossless 64 px TGA sheet from `--source`
(the `dist/TwitchEmotes-3.0.0-tga-baseline.zip` archive when present, otherwise the addon
`Media` directory) and never from a converted BLP. Each animation is snapped (alpha 5 and
below becomes 0, 250 and above becomes 255), temporally stabilised (`--hold 3`, two passes
around the loop seam, identical source frames forced identical), and folded so exact and
near-duplicate frames (`--near 3:1.0`) become one stored cell replayed through a
`sequence` list in `packs/*.json`; `fps` and the number of playback steps never change.
Every height in `--heights 64,48,40,32` crossed with every run-merge threshold in
`--merges 3,5,8` is then encoded as a candidate rung: premultiplied Lanczos resample, the
widest sheet layout the runtime accepts, a libimagequant palette without dithering, run
merging that re-points a pixel to a neighbouring or previous-frame palette index while
the added error stays under the threshold (longer deflate matches), and an indexed BLP2
with the exact 8-bit alpha plane. A rung whose visible-pixel RGB RMS error on black or
white exceeds 5/255 ships as the stabilised TGA instead. Statics keep their height and become BLP2 only when that is smaller within
the same error limit. Each rung is scored by the SSIM of its decoded
frames against the 64 px source (luma at 1440p and 40 UI units), so palette, merge, and
resample loss all count. With a `--budget`, animations start at 64 px, threshold 3, and
step down one at a time to the smaller rung with the least SSIM loss per byte saved, never
below `--floor 0.85`, until the total fits or nothing above the floor is left; the summary
and `--report` JSON show totals, the height and threshold mix, SSIM statistics, and how
many TGAs remain. Candidates are
cached in `--cache` (`.cache/optimize`) by source hash and parameters, so another budget
re-allocates without re-encoding. The optimizer updates every shared reference, records
each entry's source sheet under `lossless`, regenerates the pack Lua, and stages
replacements with rollback; `--dry-run` only measures. Output is deterministic for the
same input and parameters.

Run focused checks with `luajit tests/core_spec.lua`, `luajit tests/text_spec.lua`,
`luajit tests/runtime_spec.lua`, `luajit tests/animation_spec.lua` and `luajit tests/ui_spec.lua`.
The external WoW boundary tests complement in-client testing; they do not emulate Blizzard's
restricted execution engine or renderer, but the boundary does trace which Blizzard-owned
fields the addon writes while running insecure, and it refuses combat-restricted calls in
combat. Pass `classic` as the first argument (or set `TWITCHEMOTES_PROFILE=classic`) to run
`ui_spec` and `integration_spec` under a client shape without the Forbidden-aspect API, the
retail minimap atlas or `GetCurrentKeyBoardFocus`.
Run `luajit tests/integration_spec.lua [classic]` to load the actual manifests and all packs
through the external WoW boundary. `python3 -I scripts/api-xref.py TwitchEmotes <wowui-root> out.json`
cross-references every global, namespace member, template, event and EventRegistry callback the
runtime modules use against shallow clones of Blizzard's shipped UI source
(`github.com/Gethe/wow-ui-source`, one clone per branch under `<wowui-root>`: `live`, `classic`,
`classic_anniversary`, `classic_era`, `forever`) and flags anything a client lacks; every name it
flags today is guarded in the code. `python3 scripts/package.py` verifies every texture
hash, format, TOC reference, playback sequence, and generated Lua manifest; add
`--output dist/TwitchEmotes-3.2.1.zip` to create a release archive. Members are
deflated in parallel (`--workers`) with libdeflate level 12, zopfli, or zlib level 9,
whichever `--compressor auto` finds installed, always as an ordinary ZIP with fixed
timestamps, so one install packs to the same bytes every time. The finished archive
is reopened to confirm every member's CRC and size.
`python3 tests/test_package.py` covers that verification, each encoder, and the
archive writer.
Before a release, `python3 scripts/check-interface.py` reads the live `us` build of
`wow`, `wow_classic`, `wow_anniversary`, `wow_classic_era` and `wowf` from the
Battle.net versions endpoints, computes each interface number
(major × 10000 + minor × 100 + patch) and fails unless the client's manifest and the
fallback `TwitchEmotes.toc` in `FLAVOR_TOCS` declare it; it prints one line per client.
`python3 tests/test_check_interface.py` tests it offline.
`.venv/bin/python tests/test_texture_optimizer.py` checks format validation, transparency,
temporal cleanup, sequences, layout, allocation, shared references, quality fallback,
and repeatable conversion. Run
`python3 tests/test_pack_builder.py` after changing the builder or its publication logic.

`scripts/deploy.sh [ssh-host] [addons-dir] [--replace-foreign]` stages and verifies
every file before replacing this addon's folder. It defaults to the author's WoW Forever
client (`_forever_`) on `mizepc`; pass another client's `Interface\AddOns` path to deploy
there. It refuses a path whose client folder, two levels above `AddOns`, holds neither
`.flavor.info` nor a `Wow*.exe`, so a mistyped path creates nothing. It also refuses to
replace a `TwitchEmotes` folder whose TOC lacks `## Author: TheMizeGuy`, such as another
addon published under that folder name, unless `--replace-foreign` is given. The folder it
replaces is moved to `TwitchEmotes.previous-<yyyyMMddHHmmss>` in the same `AddOns` folder,
which the client ignores; delete it by hand once the new build works.

releases.name: Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.2.1
releases.notes:
Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.2.1 removes one channel group. It runs on WoW Forever 1.60.1, Retail 12.1.5, Mists of Pandaria Classic 5.5.4, Burning Crusade Anniversary 2.5.6, and Classic Era 1.15.9.

**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing this update.** `/reload` alone can leave emote textures as green boxes until the client restarts.

- One channel group and its 106 emote names were removed, along with one related emote that two other groups carried. The collection is now 66 groups and about 8,400 names. Your other channels and settings are unchanged.
- The space this freed went back into picture quality: 109 animations are stored at a larger frame height. The download stays under 200 MB.

releases.name: Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.2.0
releases.notes:
Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.2.0 adds a channel group and a first-login channel picker. It runs on WoW Forever 1.60.1, Retail 12.1.5, Mists of Pandaria Classic 5.5.4, Burning Crusade Anniversary 2.5.6, and Classic Era 1.15.9.

**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing this update.** `/reload` alone can leave new emote textures as green boxes until the client restarts.

- One new channel group with 565 emote names, 335 of them animated, brings the collection to 67 groups and about 8,500 names. Like every added channel it starts disabled; tick it under Channels.
- The first time you enter the world after installing, the window opens on the channel picker so you can tick the groups you want. General and five channel groups start ticked, and your existing choices are kept. The picker opens once: Finish or closing the window ends it, and the Channels tab brings it back whenever you like. It waits until you are out of combat.
- The download stays under 200 MB. To make room, 558 of the 3,082 earlier animations are stored at a smaller frame height (most by one step, 105 by two or three); no emote and no frame of timing was removed.

Every Twitch global text face (`:)`, `:-P`, `:/`, `<3`, `O_o`, `B)` and the rest), `D:`, and the chat words `1G`, `BOP`, `Retail`, and `Classic` stay disabled by default and can be restored individually.

Open the browser with `/te`, `/twitch`, or the minimap button.

releases.name: Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.1.0
releases.notes:
Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.1.0 runs on every current World of Warcraft client: WoW Forever 1.60.1, Retail 12.1.5, Mists of Pandaria Classic 5.5.4, Burning Crusade Anniversary 2.5.6, and Classic Era 1.15.9.

**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing this update.** `/reload` alone can leave new emote textures as green boxes until the client restarts.

- One download serves all five clients. Each client loads its own manifest, and the AddOn List names the game version, for example "Twitch Emotes (Classic Era)".
- Autocomplete now uses the addon's own suggestion list instead of driving Blizzard's chat autocomplete, which tainted the active chat box for the rest of the session. Up and Down move the highlight, and Tab or a click inserts the name while the chat box keeps focus. Enter always sends your message as typed, so `lol :P` goes out unchanged.
- Clicking an emote in the browser, or Shift-clicking one in chat, inserts its name only when the chat box is already open. The addon never opens chat for you.
- The emote browser and the emote menu let movement and ability keys through, in combat too.
- Minimap button collectors such as MinimapButtonButton, Leatrix Plus, and EllesmereUI can now gather the minimap button. When another addon has loaded LibDBIcon, the button takes LibDBIcon's standard look and also appears in broker displays such as Titan Panel.
- Chat matching leaves web addresses, escaped pipes, runs of punctuation, brackets, and non-English punctuation alone, and autocomplete respects the chat box's 255-byte limit.
- Hidden emotes, favorites, and usage counts survive a pack update that drops a name.
- Animation redraws a line only when one of its frames changes, and lines with more than 16 links stay still.
- Retail and Forever gain a Guild Discord channel toggle. A whisper to yourself counts once in usage statistics, and censored lines you reveal now show their emotes.

Every Twitch global text face (`:)`, `:-P`, `:/`, `<3`, `O_o`, `B)` and the rest), `D:`, and the chat words `1G`, `BOP`, `Retail`, and `Classic` stay disabled by default and can be restored individually.

Open the browser with `/te`, `/twitch`, or the minimap button.

releases.name: Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.0.1
releases.notes:
Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.0.1 is a maintenance release for WoW Forever 1.60.1.

**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing this update.** `/reload` alone can leave new emote textures as green boxes until the client restarts.

- The addon now reads and writes only its own `ForeverEmotesDB` saved variable. The one-time import of settings and usage counts from other emote addons is removed; existing 3.x preferences and statistics are kept.
- No emote, texture, or pack changed: the collection is the same 8,000+ names across 66 groups in a download under 200 MB (1.3 GB installed).

Everything else is unchanged from 3.0.0:

- Search and preview every installed group, then enable it directly from Browse.
- Favorites, recent emotes, individual hiding, and controls for shared emote names.
- Autocomplete with emote image previews and an adjustable 12–40 pixel chat size.
- Source-timed animation, visible-line updates, and a compact movable minimap button.
- General and five channel groups enabled by default, with no automatic setup popup.

Every Twitch global text face (`:)`, `:-P`, `:/`, `<3`, `O_o`, `B)` and the rest), `D:`, and the chat words `1G`, `BOP`, `Retail`, and `Classic` are disabled by default and can be restored individually.

Open the browser with `/te`, `/twitch`, or the minimap button. Use Channels or Settings > Choose channels to adjust the preset selection.

Known beta issue: the Forever client may reset addon settings after reloads or restarts. This release uses its preset selection when settings are unavailable. Manual changes work for the current session; automatic first-run setup is postponed until the client saves settings reliably.

releases.name: Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.0.0
releases.notes:
Twitch Emotes WoW Forever 3.0.0 brings animated chat emotes and a purple visual browser to WoW Forever 1.60.1.

**Fully exit and restart WoW after installing this update.** `/reload` alone can leave new emote textures as green boxes until the client restarts.

- More than 8,000 emote names across 66 groups, with one group per channel.
- Full collection in a download under 200 MB (1.3 GB installed), keeping every emote, every frame of animation, and source timing; static emotes stay at 64 px and animations use the largest frame height the budget allows, chosen per emote.
- General and five channel groups enabled by default, with no automatic setup popup.
- Search and preview every installed group, then enable it directly from Browse.
- Favorites, recent emotes, individual hiding, and controls for shared emote names.
- Autocomplete with emote image previews and an adjustable 12–40 pixel chat size.
- Source-timed animation, visible-line updates, and a compact movable minimap button.

Every Twitch global text face (`:)`, `:-P`, `:/`, `<3`, `O_o`, `B)` and the rest), `D:`, and the chat words `1G`, `BOP`, `Retail`, and `Classic` are disabled by default and can be restored individually.

Open the browser with `/te`, `/twitch`, or the minimap button. Use Channels or Settings > Choose channels to adjust the preset selection.

Known beta issue: the Forever client may reset addon settings after reloads or restarts. This release uses its preset selection when settings are unavailable. Manual changes work for the current session; automatic first-run setup is postponed until the client saves settings reliably.
